overview: Host John Petrella interviews Sam Sednick, the director of the Charlotte and William Bloomberg Medford Public Library, about his background and the library's various offerings. They discuss physical and digital resources, volunteering opportunities, and upcoming community programs.

items.title: Welcome and Director's Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduces library director Sam Sednick, who shares his professional background, including his Peace Corps service and path to directorship.

items.title: Typical Day and Digitization Projects
items.summary: Sednick outlines his daily duties and highlights the library's ongoing efforts to digitize local history and microfilm archives using software and volunteer assistance.

items.title: Makerspace and the Library of Things
items.summary: Sednick describes the crafts and equipment available in the Makerspace, as well as the 'Library of Things' which allows patrons to check out non-traditional items like kayaks, tools, and folding tables.

items.title: Modern Library Challenges
items.summary: Sednick discusses national and local challenges facing libraries, including budget constraints and debates surrounding book access and collection development.

items.title: Digital Resources and the Maker Space
items.summary: Sednick explains the online resources available to patrons, such as resume and job search help, as well as badging requirements for independent Makerspace use.

items.title: Room Reservations and Library Publications
items.summary: Sednick explains the reservation processes for the library's study rooms, Makerspace, and Bonsignore Hall, noting how they align with the library's quarterly newsletter.

items.title: Volunteer Opportunities
items.summary: Sednick details volunteer roles at the library, which include shelving books, metadata processing for local history digitization, and teaching craft classes.

items.title: Upcoming Library Events and Programs
items.summary: Sednick highlights upcoming community programs, including a library card drive in the Wellington area, a Lunch and Learn, a Coffee and Books group, historical lectures, and therapy dog programs.

items.title: Library Jingle and Teen Music Programs
items.summary: Sednick plays a library jingle created by local teens and details the digital music, podcasting, and recording resources available to youth at the library.

items.title: Closing Announcements
items.summary: Petrella thanks Sednick and concludes the episode with closing remarks and contact information for Medford Happenings.
